sections.html:
Lowndes County is on Mississippi's eastern border with Alabama, and its county seat is Columbus. At the 2020 census it had 58,879 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 57,346, a decline of 2.6 percent. The county forms the Columbus micropolitan area and is one of three counties in the Golden Triangle region.

It covers 516 square miles, of which 506 are land and 11 are water. Its neighbors are Noxubee County to the south, Oktibbeha to the west, Clay to the northwest, Monroe to the north, and Lamar and Pickens counties in Alabama to the east. The land was fully wooded before settlement; the level areas are now cleared for farming or development, and the drainages, about 40 percent of the total area, remain wooded.

The Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway runs through the center of the county, with the John C. Stennis Lock and Dam near Columbus. US 45, US 45 Alternate, US 82 and Mississippi Highways 12, 50, 69 and 182 are the main highways.

sections.h2: Which communities and school districts are in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Columbus is the only city. The towns are Artesia, Caledonia and Crawford, and the census-designated places are Columbus Air Force Base and New Hope. Unincorporated communities include Bent Oak, Billups, Flint Hill, Forreston, Kolola Springs, Mayhew, McCrary, Penns, Plum Grove, Steens, Trinity, Wells, Whitebury and Woodlawn.

Two public systems serve the county. The Columbus Municipal School District runs Columbus High School, Columbus Middle School, the McKellar Technology Center and five elementary magnet schools. The Lowndes County School District has three areas, Caledonia, New Hope and West Lowndes, each with an elementary, middle and high school. Private options include Heritage Academy, Columbus Christian Academy, Victory Christian Academy and Annunciation Catholic School. The Mississippi University for Women is in Columbus.

School district boundaries matter to a property tax bill, since the state notes that county, municipal and school levies are combined in the millage rate.

sections.h2: What drives the Lowndes County economy?
sections.html:
Lowndes County combines manufacturing, a military base and a university. The Lowndes County Economic Development Commission lists American Colloid (bentonite clay), Bates Turkey Farm, Chowel Weldparts, Daehan Solutions Alabama, Findley Timber, Koch Foods, Priester Pecan, SABIC engineered plastics and Sejong Alabama among its top industries. The regional development group GTR Link says the Golden Triangle includes steel and metal, timber, aerospace, defense, automotive and technology companies.

Columbus Air Force Base, home of the 14th Flying Training Wing, sits about 8 miles north of downtown Columbus off Highway 45. Military One Source describes Columbus as a low-cost military town with many retirees.

The Golden Triangle Regional Airport completed a terminal expansion that added 8,200 square feet, according to a July 28, 2026 note from Congressman Trent Kelly.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
The Lowndes County Tax Office is at 1121 Main Street in Columbus, with the tax collector reachable at 662-329-5700. The assessor's mapping line is 662-329-3940.

sections.h2: When are Lowndes County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due on or before February 1 for property assessed in the prior year, and a February 1 that falls on a weekend or legal holiday moves to the next Monday without penalty. The state values ownership as of January 1, and bills come out in November or December.

  • January 1 to April 1: homestead exemption applications.
  • First Monday in August: normal appeal deadline with the Board of Supervisors.
  • February 1: payment due.
  • After February 1: interest of one-half of one percent per month.

Be careful with web searches for "Lowndes County tax" because a site for a similarly named county in another state shows a different due date. Use the Mississippi county's own site, lowndescountyms.com.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lowndes County assessment?
sections.html:
You request a hearing with the county Board of Supervisors through the Chancery Clerk, and the normal deadline is the first Monday in August before the tax is due.

Real property in Mississippi must be revalued at least once every four years, so your value can change when your parcel comes up for review. Interior inspections of residences are not required, and the assessor values all structures on a parcel, including outbuildings. If the size of your house was recorded wrongly, the state says a refund for prior years may be possible through the Chancery Clerk.

The assessor's staff can walk you through the value on the roll before you file. Take your photos, any recent appraisal and recent sales of similar houses with you.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Lowndes County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent property is sold at the county tax sale, and the owner has two years to redeem. A 2017 Commercial Dispatch report said Lowndes County moved its tax sale online that year through GovEase, with about 1,900 parcels carrying $1.6 million in delinquent taxes. The paper's report also said the owner who redeems pays the delinquent taxes and the buyer's money is returned with monthly interest, and that if two years pass the buyer can get a tax deed from the chancery clerk.

Those figures are old and the format may have changed, so ask the Tax Office for the current sale date. The state says sales can occur on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August. For land already sold to the state, call the Secretary of State at 1-866-835-2637.

For a Lowndes County homeowner, the simplest fix is to sell before the sale date. The title company pays the taxes from the proceeds.

sections.h2: Selling a Lowndes County house: what to line up
sections.html:
Selling in Lowndes County follows the same Mississippi steps as elsewhere: a title search, a prepared deed, payment of taxes and liens at closing, and recording with the chancery clerk.

  • Pull the parcel on the Property Link search to see the assessed value and tax status.
  • Ask the tax office for a payoff on any delinquent years.
  • Check homestead status, since an owner-occupied single-family home is assessed at 10 percent and other real property at 15 percent.
  • For inherited houses, the chancery court handles probate and the clerk files the papers.

Owners in Columbus, Caledonia, New Hope or the rural west of the county sometimes sell as-is because of repairs, a move for work, or an estate. A cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal and repair demands. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Lowndes County property individually and does not promise a price or timeline before reviewing it.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work for a Lowndes County home?
sections.html:
Homestead exemption applies to the house you live in and is filed with the tax assessor in the county where the home sits, between January 1 and April 1. You do not reapply each year, but you should refile if your marital status or ownership changes.

The Department of Revenue says homeowners 65 or older, and those who are totally disabled, can be exempt on the first $75,000 of true value if otherwise eligible. Proof of disability may include a VA release form, a Social Security benefit report or letters from two physicians. Eligibility can be lost if the owner or spouse is out of compliance with state income tax law, and a car tagged in another county can also count against you.

If you inherited a Lowndes County house and no one lives there, homestead will not apply, so the 15 percent ratio is the one to expect.

faqs.q: When are Lowndes County, MS property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 each year. If that date lands on a weekend or holiday, you can pay the next Monday without interest, and later payments add one-half of one percent per month.

faqs.q: Where is the Lowndes County Tax Office?
faqs.a: The Tax Office is at 1121 Main Street in Columbus, MS 39701, and the phone is 662-329-5700. The county also has an online payment portal for real and personal property tax and car tags.

faqs.q: What is the Lowndes County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Normally the first Monday in August before the tax is due. You request a hearing with the Board of Supervisors through the Chancery Clerk.

faqs.q: Is lowndescounty.com the Mississippi county site?
faqs.a: No. The Mississippi county's site is lowndescountyms.com. A similarly named site for a county in another state lists a different due date.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lowndes County house if taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the back taxes from your proceeds at closing. If the property has been sold at a tax sale, you can still redeem within two years of the sale.
